svg_description: The service-flow model is a verified mirror compared with the deployment dependency map by a parity check. The deployment dependency map and runtime identity feed the IAM grant plan; deployment applies those grants for Cloud IAM enforcement. In a separate lane, a name-set check compares declared deployment names with the observed fleet. That comparison is not verification of IAM bindings.

caption: Supported typed edits share a controlled application path. A pipeline, agent, or human editor can propose changes against the document model. The PDF applier checks selected restrictions and applies or refuses operations individually; results and applied-edit attribution describe what occurred. Some internal remediation still edits directly. [short: The controlled typed-editing path]
conversion: TikZ diagram; inspect SVG and chapter/receipt
svg_title: Supported typed edits cross a common controlled application boundary
svg_description: A document model supplies structure and semantics to edit producers: a structured pipeline, an agent, or a human editor. Supported proposals are encoded as typed changesets with kind, target, and payload. The controlled PDF applier resolves targets, checks selected restrictions, and applies or refuses each operation. Its outputs are an updated document and application evidence: per-operation results plus attribution for edits actually applied. This is the controlled editing path; some internal remediation paths still mutate documents directly.

caption: A structured work order selects applicable engineering knowledge from maintained models. Brief validation precedes dispatch; the agent implements and commits. Completion review compares landed work and independent check evidence with the work order, then updates its status. An agent report alone does not establish completion. [short: Model-guided delegation and completion evidence]
